headline: Sodium-ion batteries closing in on lithium's cost advantage
meta_description: Sodium-ion battery costs have fallen dramatically and may reach €28.5–51.9/kWh by 2050, challenging lithium's dominance in energy storage.
summary_short: Sodium-ion batteries hit €120/kWh in 2025 and could plummet to a quarter of that by 2050, reshaping the future of renewable energy storage.
body:
Sodium-ion batteries have reached system-level costs of around €120 per kilowatt-hour of capacity in 2025—close enough to lithium to signal a genuine shift in battery economics.

Projections suggest these costs could fall dramatically to between €28.5 and €51.9 per kilowatt-hour by 2050. That trajectory matters because cost has long been the barrier keeping sodium-ion technology on the sidelines, despite its advantages in abundance and safety.

The significance lies not in sodium replacing lithium overnight, but in what cost parity means: real choice. As production scales and manufacturing improves, sodium-ion batteries won't need to be a compromise solution. They become a viable option for stationary storage, vehicles, and grid applications—especially in regions where lithium supply is tight. That flexibility is what reshapes markets.
quick_facts: Challenge to lithium's market dominance underway
